channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO May See CBA Sitting on Multi-Billion Windfall
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering may give Commonwealth Bank of Australia an opportunity to cash in on a stake it purchased in the artificial intelligence startup more than a year ago and whose valuation has ballooned.
item.dc:creator: Richard Henderson

item.title: BNY CFO on AI Strategy, Business Growth
item.description: Dermot McDonogh, Global CFO at BNY, discusses his outlook on the bank's growth and business strategies, as well as how he is monitoring AI so as to avoid overspending on related tools. He speaks exclusively with Paul Allen and Haidi Stroud Watts on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BlackRock’s Rieder Spent All Weekend Doing Deals in AI Debt Rush
item.description: The AI-driven debt boom is creating some of the most attractive fixed-income opportunities in years, eclipsing the appeal of long-dated US Treasuries, according to BlackRock’s Rick Rieder.
item.dc:creator: Haidi Lun, Paul Allen and David Finnerty

item.title: AI Fund a ‘Fiscal Dam’, Says South Korea Budget Minister
item.description: In an exclusive conversation with Bloomberg's Heesu Lee, South Korean budget minister Park Hong Keun says that the fund financed by semiconductor-driven tax gains will serve as a fiscal dam to cushion from higher yields (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Fund a ‘Fiscal Dam’, Says South Korea Budget Minister
item.description: In an exclusive conversation with Bloomberg's Heesu Lee, South Korean budget minister Park Hong Keun says that the fund financed by semiconductor-driven tax gains will serve as a fiscal dam to cushion from higher yields (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: South Korea’s AI Fund Offers ‘Fiscal Dam’ Against Higher Yields
item.description: As nations across the globe grapple with a surge in borrowing costs, almost none enjoy the option now being eyed in South Korea: deploying a major new source of cash to simply cut back on selling debt.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee and Jaehyun Eom

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Sets Up Defining Moment for Wall Street and AI Boom
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering is laying bare the extremes of the multi-trillion-dollar AI boom business model: extraordinary growth paired with uncertainty about demand and the spending required to continue developing the technology. The startup, which publicly filed IPO paperwork on Monday, is poised to be the first major US firm focused solely on building AI software to make its market debut.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Iran War Boosts Malaysian Data Center Appeal, SD Guthrie Says
item.description: Malaysia is expected to attract more interest as a data center hub following the outbreak of the US-Iran war, according to SD Guthrie Bhd., giving the palm oil giant and the country’s biggest landowner an opportunity to capitalize on the boom.
item.dc:creator: Anuradha Raghu and Ram Anand

item.title: The High Price of India’s iPhone Manufacturing Boom
item.description: India now makes one in four iPhones, but its dependence on imported components remains substantial. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Andy Mukherjee says the country's manufacturing gains may not justify the growing taxpayer subsidies needed to replicate China's success. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spain Eases Data Center Energy Rules in Win for Big Tech
item.description: Spain is easing rules for data center power usage after an initial government proposal faced strong industry backlash.
item.dc:creator: Clara Hernanz Lizarraga

item.title: AirTrunk Secures $3 Billion Green Loan for Sydney Data Center
item.description: AirTrunk secured a A$4.25 billion ($3 billion) green loan to finance the development of a Sydney data center campus, a signal of confidence in a sector that’s taken a slew of hits in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Adam Haigh

item.title: SVP’s Khosla: Credit Markets Have a Lot of Tail Risk
item.description: Victor Khosla, Founder and CIO of Strategic Value Partners, discusses headwinds worsening since his previous appearance. While markets have already repriced amid mounting pressure, he says risks remain unusually high: whereas he would normally put the chance of severe tail events at about 5%, he estimates a 20% to 30% chance that such risks could materialize now. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ValueEdge’s Minow on Anthropic’s Share Class Structure
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO filing outlines a governance structure in which seven cofounders direct Class F shares representing about 50.1% of total voting power on key issues. Nell Minow, Chair at ValueEdge Advisors, says the filing asks investors to trust a multilevel structure: an independent board would appoint most directors, while the founders retain controlling votes. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: AI Agents Are Already Changing the Price of Goods
item.description:
With the release of AI agents like Meta's Muse, tech companies are promising consumers that they will start saving them tons of money by finding the best deals.
On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, President and CEO of Groundwork Collaborative Lindsay Owens joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to discuss her think tank's research into agentic commerce and how agents may not be operating in the best interest of the consumer. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Applied Materials Boosts BE Semiconductor Stake to About 20%
item.description: Applied Materials Inc. boosted its stake in fellow chip-equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries NV and vowed to step up their work together, citing the European company’s growing role in energy-efficient AI computing.
item.dc:creator: Nick Turner

item.title: Anthropic Warns of Existential Risk, Liability and Slowing Sales
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s filing for a landmark initial public offering included nearly 100 pages of risk factors, an unusually exhaustive set of disclosures for how the company’s artificial intelligence business could go awry.The list included everything from slowing revenue growth and government regulation to “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.” The scope of the risks hints at unique challenge public market investors face in gauging the promise and peril of Anthropic’s technology.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary and Rachel Metz

item.title: Netflix Hires Former Apple Executive to Oversee Podcasts
item.description: Steve Wilson joins the streamer in its nascent efforts to push into video podcasts.
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: SK Hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, CXMT Earnings Test AI Boom in Memory Market
item.description: From South Korea to Japan and China, the world’s biggest memory chipmakers will this week seek to quell fears that AI spending is outpacing future demand. How they handle back-to-back earnings disclosures and investors’ questions will help determine the trajectory for markets and shed light on the broader outlook for the artificial intelligence industry.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Winnie Hsu

item.title: Instacart to Wind Down Smart Cart Business Amid Sale Talks
item.description: Instacart will stop offering high-tech shopping carts to grocers, its first announced strategy shift since reports emerged that the company is in talks to sell itself.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Intel to Acquire Startup Classiq in Quantum Computing Push
item.description: Intel Corp. agreed to buy Israeli startup Classiq Technologies Ltd. as part of a push to capitalize on quantum computing, a still-nascent field that is seeking commercial applications.
item.dc:creator: Ian King
